chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, all from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, raised it, saying:

While the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) was sitting, a nude woman came until she stood before him, so she said, 'O Messenger of Allah, I have committed fornication, so purify me.' He said. And a man came running after her and threw a cloak over her. So he (peace be upon him) said, 'And what is she to you?' So he said, 'My companion, O Messenger of Allah. I was alone with my slave girl, so she did what you see.' So he (peace be upon him) said, 'Keep her close to you.' Then he said, 'Indeed, the jealous one cannot distinguish between the top of the valley and the bottom of it.'

key_terms.طَهِّرْنِي: Purify me (referring to the punishment of flogging)

ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of the Prophet's statement about the jealous person not seeing the top and bottom of the valley?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) responds to a woman seeking purification after fornication by accepting the claim of her master who followed her, thereby avoiding public exposure and preserving her dignity. The Prophet’s advice to 'keep her close' is contextualized by the metaphor that a person with *ghayrah* (propriety/jealousy) cannot see the farthest point of the valley, illustrating that modesty involves a focused, protective concern rather than exhaustive surveillance. This highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on *ghayrah* as a virtue of preserving honor through discretion rather than public shaming.
